title: Heilbronn's Problem in the Unit Triangle: Certified Optimal Configurations for up to $n\le 8$
summary: We study Heilbronn's triangle problem in the unit right triangle, where $n$ points are placed to maximize the smallest of the $\binom{n}{3}$ triangle areas they span. We prove a boundary-structure result: unless all three vertices are occupied, some optimal configuration with $n \ge 5$ has at least four points on the boundary, one edge carrying two of them.
